text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwean press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe has overturned a multi-million deal in which retired army General Solomom Mujuru was to buy a large stake in ferrochrome company Zimasco, and has ordered the foreign owners of the firm to resume negotiations with the government to localise the company, or risk having it taken over by the state.
- President Robert Mugabe has rejected South Africa's request to free five jailed saboteurs convicted for the bombings of former African National Congress houses in Zimbabwe during the apartheid era.

- Ruling ZANU-PF party legislators on Wednesday refused to ratify loans for the construction of a new terminal at Harare International Airport, telling the government to renegotiate the financing package for the Z$1.2 billion project, in which President Robert Mugabe's nephew Leo has a stake.
- The government-owned Zimbabwe Mining Development Corporation, dogged by financial woes, made a Z$13 million net loss for the year ended June 30, 1996.
- Zimbabwe's small claims court has thrown out an application by a Harare man seeking a refund of cash which he had invested in a money club, saying there was no legal basis for the claim.
- Zimbabwe's Grain Marketing Board is to borrow Z$540 million from the local money market to buy 450,000 tonnes of maize from farmers this year.

- Chief executive of the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries, Joe Foroma, on Wednesday called on the government to pass on some of its revenue base to municipal authorities to allow them to provide adequate services to their residents.
